manifest.name: @ds-hu/dsh-auto-task-center
manifest.description: Task Center for the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI: create and manage Host-wide scheduled and webhook tasks from the right sidebar, delivered into a new session in any workspace or into an existing session, plus a 任务管理 agent preset.

scripts.test: npm run test:unit && npm run test:mount && npm run test:client
scripts.check: npm run lint && npm test && npm run test:pack

bundle.text:
# The @ds-hu/dsh-auto-task-center bundle patch.
#
# One row: the Host half. `name` must be this package's name so the Loader
# resolves the row (and therefore the code it mounts) from the profile's
# node_modules; `id` must equal the `name` the Host half exports from
# lib/index.js, so the row and the plugin are recognizably the same thing.
# Both parity rules are guarded by test/mount-check.mjs.
#
# The plugin publishes no Cordis service, so it sits loose in the Host root
# realm instead of an `isolate` group. Its data lives in
# $DSH_HOME/task-center/ and nowhere else — see docs/TECHNICAL.md#uninstall.
#
# The second patch file, presets/task-center.patch.yml, declares the 任务管理
# agent preset. Both are listed in package.json `dsh.bundle.patch`, in order.

- insert:
    - id: dsh-auto-task-center
      name: '@ds-hu/dsh-auto-task-center'

# Agent preset 任务管理 (task-center): the shipped `standard` preset with exactly one
# difference — the official reminder tools are gone and the Task Center tool is here.
#
# `config.plugins` is a COMPLETE child list; presets do not inherit. This file is a
# verbatim copy of @deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app/presets/standard.patch.yml with the
# `tool-schedule` row replaced by `task-center-tools`. When DSH updates `standard`, copy
# the new list again — docs/TECHNICAL.md#preset-sync records the procedure and
# test/mount-check.mjs fails if the row count or either marker row drifts.
#
# `name` is a single untranslated string: a plugin-shipped preset cannot be localized
# (dsh-agent-preset-registry only translates its four built-in ids), so 任务管理 shows
# verbatim in both the Chinese and the English interface.

- insert:
    - id: preset-task-center
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset'
      config:
        id: task-center
        name: 任务管理
        description: '任务中心：定时与 Webhook 任务（Task Center: scheduled and webhook tasks）'
        order: 5
        plugins:
          - id: persona
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona'
            config:
              prefix: You are a coding agent powered by the {{model}} model.
          - id: agent-instructions
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-instructions'
            config:
              maxBytes: 65536
          - id: time-context
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-time-context'
          - id: tool-bash
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-bash'
            disabled: !!js process.platform === 'win32'
          - id: tool-pwsh
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-pwsh'
            disabled: !!js process.platform !== 'win32'
          - id: tool-fs
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs'
          - id: tool-fs-search
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs-search'
            config:
              sampleOverCapGlobResults: false
          - id: tool-jobs
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-jobs'
          # Replaces the official @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-schedule row: this preset gets the
          # Task Center tool instead of the four session-bound schedule_* tools.
          - id: task-center-tools
            name: '@ds-hu/dsh-auto-task-center/tools'
          - id: skill-filesystem
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem'
          - id: tool-skill
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-skill'
          - id: command-goal
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-command-goal'
          - id: tool-goal
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-goal'
          - id: planning
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              planMode: true
            config:
              - id: plan-mode
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-plan-mode'
                config:
                  section: |
                    You are in plan mode. Stay in plan mode until the user approves your plan through exit_plan_mode or switches the session mode. Imperative language to implement changes means plan the implementation, not execute it. A user's conversational agreement — including an answer confirming something you asked — approves nothing and does not end plan mode; fold the confirmed decision into the plan and submit it through exit_plan_mode.

                    Explore first. Use non-mutating reads, searches, static analysis, and checks to ground the plan in the actual repository. Do not edit or write files, change configuration, run formatters or code generation that rewrites tracked files, commit, or otherwise carry out the plan. Prefer existing functions and patterns over new machinery.

                    The tool catalog stays the same across modes for request-cache stability. These plan-mode rules override any later tool description or guidance that suggests using mutation tools; those tools remain listed to keep the tool catalog unchanged. Do not use todo_write to track this planning phase: it tracks implementation after an approved plan, while the plan itself belongs in exit_plan_mode.

                    Resolve discoverable facts by inspection. Use ask_user_question only for user-owned choices or material ambiguity that inspection cannot answer. Do not ask the user where code lives or how current behavior works when you can find out.

                    Make the plan decision-complete: state the goal and success criteria; group implementation changes by subsystem; identify public API, schema, and data-flow changes; cover edge cases, failure modes, tests, acceptance criteria, and explicit assumptions. Keep it concise enough to review but detailed enough that another engineer can implement it without making design decisions.

                    When ready, call exit_plan_mode with the complete plan markdown, starting with a # title. Make exit_plan_mode the only and final tool call in that assistant response: it presents the plan for approval, and implementation begins only in a later step after approval. Do not paste the final plan as a plain reply or ask "should I proceed?" through prose or ask_user_question. If review rejects it, incorporate the feedback and present again. If the review channel is unavailable or aborted, stay in plan mode and ask the user to switch modes manually; do not proceed with implementation.
          - id: compaction
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              compaction: true
              toolResultPruner: true
            config:
              - id: compaction-basic
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic'
              - id: command-compact
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-command-compact'
              - id: tool-result-pruner
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-tool-result-pruner'
                config:
                  thresholdChars: 8192
                  headChars: 4096
                  tailChars: 1024
          - id: delegation
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              workflowEngine: true
            config:
              - id: tool-subagent-control
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control'
              - id: tool-subagent-list-agents
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control/list-agents'
              - id: tool-subagent
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: spawn
                  toolName: subagent
                  modelSelectionSettings: true
              - id: tool-subagent-fork
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: fork
                  toolName: subagent_fork
              - id: workflow-ptc
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-workflow-ptc'
                config:
                  provider: spawn
              - id: tool-workflow
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-workflow'
          - id: tool-ask-user
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-ask-user'
          - id: tool-todo
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-todo'
            config:
              allowParallelInProgress: true
          - id: tool-web
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-web'
            config:
              fetch: true
              searchTimeoutMs: 60000
          - id: present
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-present'
          - id: tool-plugin-manager
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-manager/tools'
            disabled: true
          - id: tool-plugin-market
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-market/tools'
            disabled: true

readme.text: **任务中心 / Task Center** — scheduled, HTTP- and hand-triggered tasks for DeepSeek Harness. Add a task once, and DSH opens a session or messages an existing one when the task fires.

中文

---

readme.section: A tab, right where you work
readme.text:
Task Center is a tab in the session's right sidebar: no new window, no separate app.
Every row answers three questions at a glance — is it on, when does it fire next, where does it deliver.
A disabled task stays in the list with its settings and history intact.

A task is caused by exactly one thing, and every row says which:

- **A schedule** — one-off, fixed interval, daily, weekly, or cron. **Next 5 runs** is computed in the time
  zone you chose, so a wrong cron expression shows up before you save it.
- **An HTTP request** — a webhook URL with its own secret, for CI, a GitHub hook, or a shell one-liner.
- **You** — a manual task has no clock and no address. It runs when you press **Run now**, and at no other time.

Running a scheduled task by hand is still a manual run, and the record says so: *Manual · Session 3f2a1c* rather than pretending the schedule fired. The agent can fire one too — `task_center` has a `run` action.

readme.section: Where it runs, on which model, with which permission
readme.text: Deliver into a **brand-new session** or into an **existing conversation**. For a new session the task decides:

readme.section: Where it runs, on which model, with which permission
Where it runs, on which model, with which permission
readme.text: The message is yours to write and arrives as a normal user message, so slash commands still work: `/goal` turns the trigger into an autonomous goal run, and any `/skill-name` loads that skill.

readme.section: Where it runs, on which model, with which permission
readme.text:
The model, effort and permission pickers appear only when the Host offers them, and leaving any of them
empty follows the deployment default. The effort list comes from the chosen model, so it can never name
something that model cannot do. If a model or preset later disappears, the task is never silently re-pointed
at something else: the run record says what failed instead of delivering into the wrong sandbox.

readme.section: Where it runs, on which model, with which permission
readme.text:
With [`dsh-better-workspaces`](https://github.com/ds-hu/dsh-better-workspaces) installed, a new session can also
land in a **fresh worktree made per run**: each run branches off the base you pick, so a nightly job never touches
the checkout you have open.

readme.section: HTTP triggers and the run record
readme.text:
An HTTP task gets its own URL and secret, on DSH's own port. The request body replaces `{{payload}}` in your
message, and **Rotate secret** makes a leaked URL useless in one click.

```bash
curl -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:3080/task-center/hook/<task-id>/<secret>" -d '{"branch":"main"}'
```

readme.section: HTTP triggers and the run record
readme.text: Every run leaves a record naming its source — schedule, HTTP, or manual: delivered, skipped because DSH was closed, or failed because the target was gone. A task that keeps failing is flagged **needs attention** instead of quietly doing nothing.

readme.section: A preset that hands scheduling to the agent
readme.text:
Installing the plugin adds an agent preset, **任务管理**: Standard mode without the built-in reminder tools, plus a
`task_center` tool — so you can say *"every weekday at 9, summarise the repo"* and the agent writes the task
itself. It can list, edit, delete, and fire one on demand.

The panel borrows DSH's theme tokens, so it looks native in light and dark alike.

---

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add @ds-hu/dsh-auto-task-center
```

Restart `dsh web`, open any session, and pick **Task Center** from the right sidebar's start page.
The **任务管理** preset shows up in the composer's mode menu.

Behind a reverse proxy, a tunnel, or Cloudflare Access, the panel keeps working: a write is checked against the
host your browser actually used, not the loopback address DSH bound.

The plugin writes only under `$DSH_HOME/task-center/` and registers no install scripts, so removing it leaves no
services, no timers and no patched configuration behind.

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove @ds-hu/dsh-auto-task-center
dsh-auto-task-center purge --yes   # optional: also delete the stored tasks
```

Move sessions off the **任务管理** preset first, then click away the one dead tab DSH keeps in your browser.
Details in [Uninstall](docs/TECHNICAL.md#uninstall).

**任务中心 / Task Center** — 给 DeepSeek Harness 加上定时、HTTP 与手动触发的任务。 设置一次，到点（或被调用时）DSH 就新建会话，或者往指定会话里发一条消息。

English

---

任务中心是会话右侧边栏里的一个标签页：不用开新窗口，点开就在旁边。
每行回答三个问题——开着吗、下次什么时候跑、跑完发到哪。停用的任务留在列表里，设置和记录都还在。

每个任务只由一种原因引起，列表里每行都写清楚是哪一种： - **时间表**——单次、固定间隔、每天、每周、Cron。**未来 5 次运行**按你选的时区算好列出来， Cron 写错了一眼就能发现，不用等它跑空。 - **HTTP 请求**——自带密钥的 Webhook 地址，给 CI、GitHub 钩子或者一行 curl 用。 - **你**——手动任务既没有时间表也没有地址，只有你点**立即运行**时才会跑，别的时候一次都不跑。

手动触发一个定时任务，也算一次手动运行，记录会写明 *手动 · 会话 3f2a1c*，而不会假装时间表跑了。 Agent 同样能触发：`task_center` 工具提供了 `run` 动作。

readme.section: 投递到哪里，用什么模型、什么权限
readme.text:
可以**新建一条会话**，也可以发到**已有会话**里。新建时这些都由任务决定： - **工作区**与 **Agent 预设**； - **模型**——想省钱就用便宜的那个，想深度推理就用最强的那个； - **思考强度**——关闭 / 低 / 高 / 最高，具体几档由所选模型决定：写摘要用便宜模型配低强度， 要动脑的重构用强模型拉满； - **权限**——仅可查看 / 工作区内修改 / 完全权限，官方那套权限预设。 它在第一次对话之前就生效，所以夜间任务从第一个动作起就被关在沙箱里。

消息完全由你写，以普通用户消息的身份进入会话，所以斜杠指令照常生效： `/goal` 让这次触发变成自主目标，`/技能名` 加载对应技能。

readme.section: 投递到哪里，用什么模型、什么权限
readme.text:
模型、思考强度与权限只在 Host 提供时才会出现在表单里；留空就是跟随部署默认。强度那一栏的选项来自
所选模型本身，不会出现它做不到的档位。哪天那个模型或预设被删了，任务不会被悄悄改成别的——
运行记录会写明失败原因，不会带病执行。

装好 [`dsh-better-workspaces`](https://github.com/ds-hu/dsh-better-workspaces) 之后，
新建会话还能落在**每次运行新建的 worktree** 里：从你指定的基分支拉一个新分支，夜里跑的 Agent 不碰你正打开的目录。

HTTP 任务有自己的地址与密钥，端口与 DSH 共用。请求体会替换消息里的 `{{payload}}`； 地址泄露了也不慌，**轮换密钥**一点，旧地址立刻失效。 ```bash curl -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:3080/task-center/hook//" -d '{"branch":"main"}' ``` 每次运行都留一条记录，并写明它是被时间表、HTTP 还是手动引起的：投递成功、DSH 没开着所以跳过、 目标没了所以失败。连续失败的任务会被标成**需处理**，而不是安静地什么都不做。

readme.section: 还给 Agent 准备了一个预设
readme.text:
装上插件，模式菜单里会多出**任务管理**：标准模式去掉官方提醒工具、加上 `task_center` 工具。
于是你可以直接说「每个工作日早上 9 点总结一下仓库」，由 Agent 自己把任务建好；
它也能列出、修改、删除任务，或者立刻跑一次。

界面跟随 DSH 的主题变量，深浅色两种模式下都像是原生的一部分。

---

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add @ds-hu/dsh-auto-task-center
```

重启 `dsh web`，打开任意会话，在右侧边栏的起始页里选 **Task Center**。
**任务管理**预设会出现在输入框的模式菜单里。

经过反向代理、隧道或者 Cloudflare Access 访问时面板照常可用：写操作校验的是浏览器实际使用的主机名，
而不是 DSH 绑定到的那串回环地址。

插件只在 `$DSH_HOME/task-center/` 下写数据，不注册安装脚本，移除后不会留下服务、定时器或被改过的配置。

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove @ds-hu/dsh-auto-task-center
dsh-auto-task-center purge --yes   # 可选：把保存的任务也删掉
```

卸载前先把还在用**任务管理**预设的会话切回别的预设；浏览器里会剩下一个点不动的标签页，点掉即可。
细节见[卸载](docs/TECHNICAL.md#uninstall)。
